keys.statement: Consider inherent safety from the first flowsheet: once technology and configuration are fixed, changes are costly, and inherently safer design is held to be the most cost-effective risk reduction.

plain.title: Consider inherent safety from the first flowsheet
plain.when: You are in conceptual design, before the route and configuration are fixed.
plain.do: Screen the routes for inherent safety now.
plain.why: Once technology and configuration are fixed, changes are costly; Park et al. 2022 hold inherently safer design to be the most cost-effective risk reduction.
plain.check: Record a safety ranking next to the cost ranking of the routes.

decisions.obstacle: Safety considered only after the route is chosen.
decisions.mechanism: Most degrees of freedom are spent before a safety review.
decisions.operation: Screen routes for inherent safety during conceptual design.

keys.statement: Prefer removing or reducing hazards (intensify, substitute, attenuate, simplify) to adding safety devices, which the authors call much less reliable.

plain.title: Remove or reduce a hazard before adding protection
plain.when: A hazard is to be handled by add-on safety devices.
plain.do: Apply the four principles when choosing operations: intensify (less hazardous inventory), substitute (a safer material), attenuate (milder conditions), simplify.
plain.why: A hazard that is not there cannot be released; Park et al. 2022 call safety devices much less reliable.
plain.check: For each hazardous stream, write down which principle was tried.

decisions.mechanism: A hazard that is not there cannot be released.
decisions.operation: Apply the four principles when choosing operations.
decisions.expected_change: Lower likelihood or consequence of incidents.

keys.statement: Rank route, unit or stream alternatives early with an index built from chemical indicators (flammability, explosiveness, toxicity) and process indicators (pressure, temperature), both known from a simple flowsheet.

plain.title: Rank alternatives early with a safety index built from chemical and process indicators
plain.when: You compare routes, units or streams on safety with little data.
plain.do: Build an index from chemical indicators (flammability, explosiveness, toxicity) and process indicators (pressure, temperature), all known from a simple flowsheet. Park et al. 2022 count 22 hazard-based, 33 risk-based and 18 cost-based tools.
plain.why: These indicators are available at the concept stage.
plain.check: Report the ranking as indicative: the indicators' weights are not yet verified against incident data.

decisions.obstacle: Comparing alternatives on safety with little data.
decisions.mechanism: Indicators available at the concept stage.
decisions.operation: Hazard-, risk- or cost-based index (22, 33 and 18 tools counted).

keys.statement: When flash point, heat of combustion or flammability limits are missing for a pure organic, simple regressions on atom counts, molar mass and normal boiling point can estimate them; the upper limit is the least reliable.

plain.title: Missing flash point or flammability limits for a pure organic: estimate them from simple correlations and label them
plain.when: Flash point, heat of combustion or flammability limits are missing for a pure organic compound.
plain.do: Estimate them with simple regressions on atom counts, molar mass and normal boiling point. Label the values as estimated and replace them with data later.
plain.why: The correlations use molecular data that are readily known.
plain.check: Treat the upper flammability limit with most caution, as it is the least reliable, and keep estimated and measured values apart.

decisions.obstacle: Missing hazard properties at the concept stage.
decisions.mechanism: Correlations from readily known molecular data.
decisions.operation: Estimate, label as estimated, and replace with data later.
limits: Estimated values are derived quantities; keep them apart from measured ones (AGENTS.md).

keys.statement: Mixture flammability does not follow the pure components proportionally and there are few data to check it against, so treat mixture estimates with caution.

plain.title: Mixture flammability: treat estimates with caution
plain.when: You estimate the hazard of a process stream that is a mixture.
plain.why: Mixture flammability does not follow the pure components proportionally, and few data exist to check it.
plain.check: Look for measured data on the actual mixture before relying on an estimate.

decisions.obstacle: Hazard of process streams that are mixtures.

keys.statement: Judge safety together with life-cycle cost, sustainability and resilience, for example in one return-on-investment metric, rather than as a separate index alone.

plain.title: Judge safety together with cost, sustainability and resilience
plain.when: A safety index alone is used to choose a route.
plain.do: Combine safety with life-cycle cost, sustainability and resilience, for example in one return-on-investment metric.
plain.why: Design trade-offs are made under several constraints at once.
plain.check: Show how the route ranking changes when safety is included.

decisions.mechanism: Trade-offs are made under several constraints at once.
decisions.operation: Combine safety with economics in the route comparison.

keys.statement: Indices that need equipment, complexity and vulnerability data (such as the inherent system safety index) fit detailed engineering, not the early concept stage.

plain.title: Detailed safety indices belong to detailed engineering, not the concept stage
plain.when: You choose a safety method for the current stage of design.
plain.do: Use simple indicator-based indices early. Keep indices that need equipment, complexity and vulnerability data, such as the inherent system safety index, for detailed engineering.
plain.why: The data these methods need differ by stage.
plain.check: Check that the index's inputs are available at your stage.

decisions.obstacle: Choosing a safety method for the stage of design.
decisions.operation: Use simple indicator-based indices early, detailed ones later.
decisions.expected_change: A method the available data can support.
